headline: The runway teaches its own prices
lede: SKYWARD's south strip now reads itself: 150/300/450/700 painted flat on the asphalt where each zone begins, a ladder banner on your first spot entry, and a windsock that actually flies. The pad finally tells the truth about its B button.

notes.text: Zone numbers painted down the strip (glyph tops toward the approach, like real distance paint), a first-run banner of the whole ladder, and a glider hint line so all three craft get named over the airfield.
The B pad is a live verb — DROP on the drop course, RECYCLE at the apron, bare B when inert — and the windsock streams downwind with a droop at slack wind and a snap when the storm cell passes.

skywardcheck 154/154 with 51/51 mutants dead; skywardplay gained live pad-verb legs and a 390px longest-string audit — and admits its old phone audit was checking against an empty pad set, fixed by giving the browser real touch.
A pad that hides under keyboard use makes headless pad assertions vacuous: the suite context now has hasTouch and wakes the pad with a tap before it reads it.
